Hi Marcus / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. HealthNode is ready to move the lab-results pipeline into a streaming, structured-output integration with Redwood. High-level goals: low-latency streaming of incoming lab events, JSON-structured outputs for downstream normalization, and a function-calling hook to trigger our "lab-normalizer" service for post-processing.

Target go-live: 2028-06-15. First asks from our side:
- A mutual action plan (kickoff, milestones, acceptance criteria)
- A sample JSON schema we can align on (field names, types, required/optional)

I attached a short requirements summary to this email (HealthNode_requirements_summary.pdf). Can we schedule a 60-min technical kickoff next week? We prefer mornings (PDT).

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. We can absolutely get you to a June 15th go-live with a focused plan. Proposed next steps:

1) Technical kickoff (60m) — proposed slots: Tue 2028-05-23 09:00 PDT or Wed 2028-05-24 10:00 PDT. Please confirm one.
2) Deliverables before kickoff (by Mon 2028-05-22):
   - Redwood: sample streaming schema + example producer payloads (attached: redwood_sample_streaming_schema.json)
   - HealthNode: representative sample payloads and a prioritized field list (you mentioned lab IDs, timestamps, result codes, reference ranges)
3) Post-kickoff (week of 5/27): scaffolding tests, a single-day integration window for end-to-end streaming, and acceptance criteria we can sign off on.

A few design notes up-front:
- We recommend a small, stable canonical schema for streaming messages (flat top-level fields + embedded array for observations) to keep KV-cache and batching predictable.
- Tool-calling: we'll surface a function named "lab_normalizer.transform(payload)" that your service can call or Redwood can call on your behalf. We support synchronous and async invocation and automatic retry with a DLQ for failing messages.
- For structured outputs, we can enforce a JSON Schema during ingestion and emit a validation report per message (useful for acceptance tests).

I've attached a sample schema to get the conversation started. We'll bring Neha (schema & validation) and Monica (CS lead) on the kickoff. Marissa will help with success criteria and rollout timing.

If that works, I will pencil Tue 5/23 09:00 PDT and send a calendar invite with agenda.

Best,

Samantha —

Thanks for the sample payloads, these are very helpful. Confirming the plan and some concrete defaults so we can align expectations before the kickoff (calendar invite sent for Tue 2028-05-23 09:00 PDT):

Defaults / agreements:
- Retry/backoff: exponential backoff with 3 retries (initial 1s, then 2s, then 4s) for 5xx. 4xx will not be retried; failures forwarded to DLQ for manual inspection.
- Invocation pattern: async POST to your lab_normalizer endpoint with idempotency-key header. Redwood will attach X-Request-Id and expects a 202 Accepted with a callback URL OR 200 + normalized payload if synchronous.
- Validation: Redwood will enforce JSON Schema at ingestion. Validation errors will return a per-message report (schema_errors) and not be sent to tool-calling unless explicitly allowed.

Ownership and timeline:
- Redwood (Marcus) — provide final streaming schema + validation rules by Mon 2028-05-22 (done).
- HealthNode (Samantha) — provide prioritized fields and the canonical list of vendor code mappings by Fri 2028-05-26.
- Redwood (Neha) — run schema validation tests and provide a validation report by Tue 2028-05-30.
- CS (Marissa / Monica) — coordinate acceptance window during week of 6/10; aim for cutover 6/15 if tests pass.

Deliverables attached: healthnode_map_v1.xlsx (field mapping prototype). I've also linked the HubSpot deal and included the DPA/EA signing link so legal can finish quickly.

If any of the timeline items look off, call them out now and we can adjust — otherwise see you on Tue at 09:00.

Best,
